- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or neutral, model often underestimates downside risk; add downward buffer or adjust for mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85.0), model frequently overcorrects upward; cap forecast growth to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model should adjust downward with increasing weight on recent low values.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture early sharp declines; apply lagged correction: if true outcome drops >2% from 10-day average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- When sentiment history includes 1.0 (strong negative), model should not forecast upward; force downward bias or reset to 10-day moving average.
